observed_problem: The deployed application serves an empty page: the SPA shell loads and sets the document title, but mounts no markup because every JavaScript and CSS chunk it requests returns 404.
governing_requirement: UI/UX plan §6 frontend architecture; ADR-025 (a page is not implemented without browser proof)
expected_behavior: The production image serves a working Servana SPA whose entry chunk and stylesheet load successfully.
actual_behavior: GET /spa/ returns 200 with title 'Servana by Citrus' and #app innerHTML length 0. GET /assets/index-BF8ocT4d.js returns 404 with a 6659-byte Laravel HTML error body. The browser refuses to apply the stylesheet because its MIME type is text/html.
root_cause: Vite is configured with base '/' so the emitted index.html references /assets/*. Nginx mounts the bundle at /spa/ via an alias, so /assets/index-*.js resolves against the Laravel public root and falls through to the PHP front controller. The same files are served correctly at /spa/assets/*.
security_or_business_impact: No user can use the deployed application. No data is exposed; the failure is total unavailability of the frontend.
entry_condition: UI-02 begins the eight-host serving foundation
future_acceptance_test: A browser test against the built production image asserts the SPA entry chunk and stylesheet return 200 and that #app renders a non-empty landmark.
notes: First actor is UI-02 because it owns nginx and URL generation. UI-17 must re-verify at deployment closeout.

actual_behavior: GET / returns 200 with document title 'Laravel' and the unmodified Laravel scaffold markup, including a fonts.bunny.net Figtree stylesheet reference. No Servana branding is present.
root_cause: routes/web.php maps GET / to view('welcome') and resources/views/welcome.blade.php is the unmodified Laravel scaffold view. No landing route was ever implemented.
security_or_business_impact: A visitor to the product sees a framework placeholder page. No data is exposed.

future_acceptance_test: A browser test asserts the root of each configured account host returns that account's landing page and never the Laravel scaffold view.
notes: UI-06 owns the landing-page content once UI-02 makes the hosts serve it.

observed_problem: No browser evidence in this repository has ever exercised the origin the product deploys to. The entire Playwright suite runs against a vite preview server that serves the SPA bundle as the web root with a fully stubbed API.
governing_requirement: UI/UX plan §21 testing and §23 browser evidence; ADR-025
expected_behavior: At least one browser suite exercises the real served origin so a serving defect cannot pass CI.
actual_behavior: playwright.config.ts sets baseURL http://localhost:4173 with webServer 'npm run build && npm run preview'. Every existing spec inherits it. UI01-PROV-001 and UI01-PROV-002 were invisible to 846 passing Playwright tests.
root_cause: The preview server serves public/spa at / so the base-path mismatch that breaks the deployed bundle cannot occur there. The API is stubbed, so no real role resolution is exercised either.
security_or_business_impact: A whole class of serving and deployment defects can reach production with a green CI pipeline.
entry_condition: UI-16 defines the release-wide browser evidence gate
future_acceptance_test: The release browser gate runs at least the shell and entry-asset checks against the built production image origin as well as the preview origin.
notes: UI-17 must confirm at deployment closeout. UI-01 added tests/e2e/ui-01-as-built-audit.spec.ts, which probes the served origin, but only as audit evidence.

observed_problem: The local build host runs Node 24.15.0 while package.json engines declares >=20.0.0 <21, and the production image builds on node:20-alpine.
governing_requirement: Plan §7 pinned stack (A-09 / ADR-001)
expected_behavior: The declared engine range matches the toolchain that produces release artifacts.
actual_behavior: npm ci and npm run build completed on Node 24.15.0 with no engine error. The resulting Vite manifest SHA-256 43a1608ab0945da6c50d122f892afe6e49bd343317c5f976ffb5d0b2851b3f81 is byte-identical to the manifest inside the production nginx image built on node:20-alpine.
root_cause: npm does not enforce the engines field by default, so an out-of-range Node version builds silently.
security_or_business_impact: None observed. Byte-identical output across both Node majors was proven for this commit; recorded so a future divergence is not mistaken for a code change.
entry_condition: UI-17 performs production build and deployment closeout
future_acceptance_test: The release build pipeline fails when the build host Node major version is outside the declared engines range.
notes: Not currently a product defect. Recorded because provenance claims depend on it.

observed_problem: An interrupted concurrent build leaves public/spa in a silently broken state and nothing detects it.
governing_requirement: UI/UX plan §23 build provenance
expected_behavior: A partially written bundle is detectable before it is served or tested.
actual_behavior: During this audit an aborted concurrent 'npm run build' left public/spa holding index.html from one build; 251 of 259 asset files from another; and no .vite/manifest.json. The shell still served with HTTP 200 while its entry chunk 404ed. 158 route visits reported blank before the cause was found.
root_cause: vite build empties outDir before writing, so a process killed mid-write leaves the directory partially populated. Neither the preview server nor the nginx image validates that every asset referenced by index.html exists.
security_or_business_impact: A broken bundle can be built, imaged and served without any stage failing.
entry_condition: UI-17 performs production build and deployment closeout
future_acceptance_test: The build pipeline asserts every /assets URL referenced by the emitted index.html exists in the emitted bundle and that .vite/manifest.json is present.
notes: The incident trigger was environmental (a timed-out Playwright webServer left an orphaned build). The missing integrity guard is the product-side defect.

observed_problem: Every merchant-side account can navigate to the Super Administrator surface and it renders in full.
governing_requirement: ADR-017 (hostnames are never authorization); UI/UX plan §4 and §18; Plan §10.2 authority boundaries
expected_behavior: A merchant-side account requesting a Super Administrator route is refused or redirected to its own account experience.
actual_behavior: All seven merchant-side accounts requested /platform and the router rendered the Super Administrator landing (landmark: 'Run your service-business platform with clarity and control.'). In the opposite direction super_administrator requesting /merchant is correctly redirected to /.
root_cause: The /platform layout record declares beforeEnter [requiresAuth] only. A requiresRole guard exists in router/guards.ts but is never applied to the platform route tree. Merchant-side trees additionally carry requiresActiveMerchant, which is why the reverse direction is refused.
affected_accounts: merchant_administrator; merchant_branch; merchant_human_resource; merchant_finance; merchant_front_office; merchant_personnel; merchant_audit
security_or_business_impact: UX-level cross-role surface exposure. Backend authorization remains the security boundary and was neither weakened nor tested here; the platform API enforces ResolvePlatformContext and EnsurePermission independently. The rendered surface still discloses the Super Administrator information architecture and navigation to every merchant role.
entry_condition: UI-03 owns authentication, session and account resolution
future_acceptance_test: A browser test asserts each of the seven merchant-side accounts requesting a /platform route is refused or redirected and never renders the Super Administrator shell.
notes: UI-08 must re-verify when it implements the Super Administrator pages. Backend enforcement is proven separately by the authorization suites and is outside UI-01 scope.

observed_problem: Any unknown path renders the Home entry card with HTTP 200 and no not-found signalling, so a missing page is indistinguishable from a working one.

root_cause: The catch-all route is deliberately mapped to Home.vue, and the screen inventory records the same component for both the home and not-found keys.

observed_problem: The operating-system colour scheme selects the theme: a user with a dark OS preference and no stored Servana preference gets dark mode at first paint.
governing_requirement: ADR-021 (light mode is the default; prefers-color-scheme must not select the theme); CLAUDE.md guardrail 15
expected_behavior: Light mode is the default. prefers-color-scheme is never consulted. Dark mode is explicit and persistent per browser when anonymous and per user record when authenticated.
actual_behavior: With colorScheme dark and no stored preference the root element carried class 'dark' at first paint and rendered dark. The pre-hydration script reads window.matchMedia('(prefers-color-scheme: dark)') and applies the dark class when no stored value exists. The other four scenarios behaved correctly.
root_cause: The pre-hydration theme script applies dark when 'stored' is absent and 'prefersDark' is true. The condition should depend on the stored value alone.
security_or_business_impact: Every anonymous visitor on a dark-preference device sees a theme the product does not default to. Contrast and brand expression were designed light-first.
entry_condition: UI-04 delivers the design system and theme
future_acceptance_test: A browser test asserts that with prefers-color-scheme dark and no stored preference the root element carries no dark class at first paint and the rendered theme is light.
notes: Persistence per authenticated user record is separately owned by UI-03 and was not exercised here.

observed_problem: The built SPA references favicon URLs that do not exist under its own web root, so they 404 on the preview origin.
governing_requirement: UI/UX plan §23 browser evidence
expected_behavior: The bundle references assets that resolve on every origin it is served from.
actual_behavior: The built index.html references /assets/brand/favicon.ico and three sibling icons. Vite has no publicDir (resources/spa/public does not exist) so these files are absent from public/spa and 404 on the preview origin. They resolve on the served origin only because the Laravel public root also owns /assets.

observed_problem: No FAQ surface exists for any of the eight accounts, and requesting one renders a broken state rather than a not-found page.
governing_requirement: UI/UX plan §6 (every account has a role-specific FAQ); CLAUDE.md section 3A
expected_behavior: Each account has a reachable FAQ page rendered verbatim from its source document.

observed_problem: Twelve routes throw an uncaught TypeError while rendering because nested payload fields are dereferenced without a guard.
governing_requirement: UI/UX plan §9 design system and §21 testing; Plan §11.5 error envelope
expected_behavior: A screen renders a defined empty or error state when a payload field is absent rather than throwing.
actual_behavior: Under the repository's own canonical e2e fixtures these routes each logged a TypeError: /branch/cash-up (reading find, twice); /finance/cash-up/{id}; /finance/invoices/{id}; /finance/payment-records/{id}; /finance/receipts/{id}; /finance/refunds/{id}; /front-office/invoices/{id}; /front-office/receipts/{id} (reading formatted); /front-office/payments/record/{id} (reading amount); /merchant/compensation-summary and /personnel/earnings (reading length); /merchant/subscription (reading name). All twelve still rendered a landmark, so the failure is confined to a child component.
root_cause: These components dereference nested money and collection fields directly. The repository's shared e2e fixtures omit those fields for the detail routes, so the dereference throws. Whether a production API response can omit them is a separate question the owning phase must settle against the backend contract.
security_or_business_impact: A partially rendered screen with a silent console failure. No data is exposed. Severity would rise if the production API can emit the same shape.
entry_condition: UI-04 delivers the shared components these screens render money and collections through
future_acceptance_test: Each affected route renders with an incomplete payload and produces no uncaught exception, showing a defined empty state instead.
notes: First actor is UI-04 because the money and table primitives are shared. UI-10, UI-12, UI-13 and UI-14 re-verify their own routes. The API-shape question may require a backend decision.
